requirements.notes: Measured locally (evidence is produced on the integration branch): shared_primitive_kinds 20 of 20 (every owner module and table present, no duplicate facts in any of the 74 4.0 families), cross_module_rollback_failures 0 over 240 randomised six-module commands failing in 7 real ways plus 20 contained failing sub-calls, inference_replay_without_rerun true (48 recorded torch-MLP cohort decisions with OS-entropy sampling; 0 network calls during regeneration and replay, both exact).

The execution-mode registry exists and checks every provider for real (two builds from one seed, identical results; kernel worlds also replayed). Measured execution_modes = 1: Mode A via the 4.0 hidden-mechanism families (crucible.mechanisms, 25 environments). Modes B (crucible.domains, workstream I) and C (crucible.civ, workstream J) have no provider yet; the gate test records the number without asserting the >= 3 threshold.

limitations: Bytes uploaded through the artifact.put tool are also in the recorded cmd event (arguments are recorded for regeneration); module code should store large media with artifacts.put, whose events hold only the REF.
Store-less worlds keep artifact bytes in a process-wide content-addressed pool for the life of the process; long or large runs should use a store.
A world moved to another store must run artifacts.export(world, dest_store) before it is loaded in another process; in-process forks and replays find their parent's blobs automatically.
columns.declare runs in Module.install, so loading a snapshot briefly allocates the declared fill arrays before the snapshot's arrays replace them.
Subscribers never run in the rejection transaction (cmd.rejected and persisted refusal events).

Typed events cover the 5.0 substrate types and 21 events of the 4.0 primitive owners (primitives.PRIMITIVE_EVENTS, checked against 4.0 logs); other 4.0 event types are untyped, and sched.add is validated by tests only (kernel commit-path types cannot carry subscribers).

relationship and community are owned by the 4.0 forum tables and product by market.listings; moving ownership to v5 social/commerce modules is a registry change in primitives.OWNERS. market.inventory vs industry.stock is reported as a recognised 4.0 overlap (warning).
SP-2.1 criterion (>= 3 operational modes) is not met until workstreams I and J register Mode B and C providers.
integration_notes: Kernel extension points (byte-identical for 4.0 worlds, proven by tests/test_v5_substrate_kernel.py against digests recorded on c07098b and by tests/test_behavior.py): World.subscribers/_notify, Ctx.quiet, World.replay(store=...), StateStore.array_rows_mut, StateStore.declaring/declared_by.
services/identity.py resolve_handle: a population principal 'p<i>' resolves to itself (one line; 4.0 resolution unchanged because 4.0 person ids always contain ':').

sandbox/bridge.py: the deterministic line count now sets aside gc callbacks installed by other code while counting (found by the regression run: tests/test_scale.py failed after tests/test_kernel_props.py because hypothesis' gc timer callback ran inside a measured region). 4.0 processes have no gc callbacks, so 4.0 digests are unchanged (tests/test_behavior.py, tests/test_v5_substrate_kernel.py).

Population (B): list modules 'artifacts' and 'cols' in the spec, depend on 'cols', call columns.declare(world, 'pop', n, {...}) and attention.declare(world, n) (or include attention.COLUMNS) in install, attention.reset(ctx) daily, columns.batch for every cohort update, ids.ensure_principal(ctx, i, account=True) for individuals that transact.

Social (C), commerce (F), innovation (G): declare shared facts with a class attribute shared_facts = {kind: table} only for kinds you own (primitives.OWNERS); to own relationship/community/product/tool_definition with new tables, ask workstream A to move ownership; check with primitives.check_no_duplicates(world).

Semantic (D): recorded(ctx, kind, model_id, weights_hash(model), inputs, fn) returns read-only numpy arrays when fn returns an array or a dict of arrays (stored as an array blob; needs the artifacts module); JSON outputs go into the ext record.

Tiers (H, I, J): register execution-mode providers from your package's modules.py: modes.register('A'|'B'|'C', name, package=..., names=..., make=..., kind='env'|'world'|'sim', check=optional); modes.status() runs them.

Cross-module couplings: bus.subscribe(world, '<host>.<what>', fn, owner=module_name) in Module.install; fn(ctx, ev) runs as sys inside the emitting transaction after the applier; raising undoes the whole command.
